台风般的

senses.title: Tropical cyclone of the western Pacific
senses.titleCN: 台风：西北太平洋的热带气旋
senses.definition: a tropical cyclone that forms in the western North Pacific or the South China Sea
senses.definitionCN: 在西北太平洋或南海生成的热带气旋
senses.example: The typhoon gathered strength over the warm Kuroshio current.
senses.exampleCN: 台风在温暖的黒潮上空积蓄力量。
senses.why: This is the technical sense: a warm-core storm whose winds circle a low-pressure eye.
senses.whyCN: 这是技术义：一个暖核风暴，风绕着低压眼区旋转。

senses.title: The Pacific name for a hurricane
senses.definition: the basin-specific name for a storm that Atlantic forecasters would call a hurricane
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋预报员称为飓风的同一类风暴在太平洋海域的名称
senses.example: The same storm would be called a typhoon west of the date line.
senses.exampleCN: 同一场风暴在日期变更线以西就会被称为台风。
senses.why: Basins keep separate naming lists, so the label changes with longitude while the physics does not.
senses.whyCN: 各海域各有命名表，因此名称随经度改变，而物理机制不变。

senses.title: A landfall disaster
senses.definition: the storm viewed as the event that brings storm surge, landslides and flooding to a coast
senses.definitionCN: 从给海岸带来风暴潮、滑坡与洪水的灾害事件角度看的台风
senses.example: The typhoon flooded the low-lying districts within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 台风在几小时内淹没了低洼城区。
senses.why: News and insurance talk about the event, so the word shifts from the system to its consequences.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与保险谈的是事件，因此这个词从天气系统转向其后果。

senses.title: Any violent windstorm in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法：泛指猛烈的风暴
senses.definition: in older literary and nautical writing, any violent revolving storm at sea
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文学与航海文字中，泛指海上任何猛烈的旋转风暴
senses.example: Sailors in the old logs feared every typhoon as a matter of course.
senses.exampleCN: 旧航海日志里的水手理所当然地畏惧每一场风暴。
senses.why: Before storms were classified by basin, the word covered any great tempest, and that broad sense survives in literary prose.
senses.whyCN: 在按海域分类之前，这个词涵盖任何大风暴，这一宽泛义仍留在文学语言里。

senses.title: The yearly typhoon season
senses.definition: the annual period, roughly summer and autumn, when typhoons are most frequent
senses.definitionCN: 台风最频繁的年度时段，大致为夏秋两季
senses.example: Building work stops during the typhoon season.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑施工在台风季停工。
senses.why: The word names the season by its dominant weather, a common pattern with weather nouns.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用主导天气给季节命名，这是天气名词常见的模式。

senses.title: A sheltered anchorage
senses.titleCN: 避风塘：供船只避风的港湾
senses.definition: a harbour or cove where boats take refuge from a storm, as in the Hong Kong place name Typhoon Shelter
senses.definitionCN: 船只躲避风暴的港湾或小湾，如香港地名中的「避风塘」
senses.example: The fishing fleet waited out the storm in a typhoon shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船队在避风塘里等风暴过去。
senses.why: A place gets its name from the weather it defends against, and the phrase became a fixed noun.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方以它所抵御的天气得名，这个短语便固定成了名词。

senses.title: Figurative storm of criticism
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：批评或情绪的暴风
senses.definition: a sudden, overwhelming outburst of criticism, anger or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 批评、愤怒或情绪的突然而压倒性的爆发
senses.example: A typhoon of criticism met the proposal on social media.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提案在社交媒体上遭遇了一场批评的暴风。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the storm's force and spin: it arrives suddenly and leaves nothing standing.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了风暴的力量与旋转：突然到来，所过之处一片狼藉。

senses.title: Official warning signals
senses.definition: the numbered signal hoisted by weather services to warn of approaching typhoon winds
senses.definitionCN: 气象部门为预警逼近的台风风力而悬挂的编号信号
senses.example: Schools closed when the typhoon signal reached the highest level.
senses.exampleCN: 台风信号升到最高级别时学校停课。
senses.why: The signal is named for the storm it announces, so the word also appears in the fixed administrative phrase.
senses.whyCN: 信号以它所预告的风暴命名，因此这个词也出现在固定的行政用语里。

intro.en: Typhoon reached English through Portuguese, and the chain behind it runs to Arabic and probably to Greek. A resemblance to a Chinese word for 'great wind' is real but its role is disputed, so this entry separates what is established from what is only suggested.
intro.cn: typhoon 经葡萄牙语进入英语，其上游可追到阿拉伯语，并很可能再追到希腊语。它与汉语中表示「大风」的词形相似确实存在，但作用有争议，因此这里把已确立的部分与仅为推测的部分分开说明。

items.en: Greek Typhōn was the name of a monstrous storm-giant, and the common noun typhōn could mean a whirlwind; its link to typhein 'to smoke' is often proposed but not certain.
items.cn: 希腊语 Typhōn 是风暴巨人提丰的名字，普通名词 typhōn 可指旋风；它与 typhein「冒烟」的联系常被提出，但并不确定。

items.en: Arabic ṭūfān means 'deluge, flood, storm'. Whether it is inherited within Arabic or borrowed from Greek typhōn is disputed.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 ṭūfān 意为「洪水、暴雨、风暴」。它是阿拉伯语内部继承还是借自希腊 typhōn，存在争议。

items.en: Portuguese tufão 'typhoon' is the immediate source for English, taken from Arabic during the age of Indian Ocean trade.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 tufão「台风」是英语的直接来源，印度洋贸易时代从阿拉伯语借入。

items.en: English records the word in the late sixteenth century in accounts of voyages to the East; early spellings vary between tufan, tuffon and typhon.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪晚期的东方航行记载中收录此词；早期拼写有 tufan、tuffon、typhon 等变体。

items.en: The modern spelling resembles Cantonese tai fung 'great wind', and some writers treat Chinese as a second source. Standard references regard the resemblance as parallel rather than proven, so the origin is not settled on this point.
items.cn: 现代拼写与粤语「大风」相近，有些作者把汉语视为第二来源。通行词源资料认为这只是并行相似而非已证实的来源，因此这一点上来源不确定。

note.en: Group one collects words that merely look or sound like typhoon; group two collects the basin names and the smaller vortices.
note.cn: 第一组只是形音相近的词；第二组是各海域的名称与更小的涡旋。

entries.definition: From Japanese taikun 'great lord': a wealthy business leader. The ending is -coon, not -phoon, and the root is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 来自日语 taikun「大君」：指富有的商界巨头。词尾是 -coon 而非 -phoon，词根无关。

entries.definition: From Greek typhos 'smoke, stupor', the name of a infectious fever; the root is smoke, not a storm.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 typhos「烟、昏沉」，是一种传染性热病的名称；词根是烟，不是风暴。

entries.definition: typhos 'smoke, stupor' plus -oid 'like'; it names a fever and shares no storm meaning.
entries.definitionCN: typhos「烟、昏沉」加 -oid「像」；指一种热病，没有风暴义。

entries.definition: The Greek proper name and common noun behind the modern word, kept in English mainly for the mythological giant.
entries.definitionCN: 现代词背后的希腊专名与普通名词，英语中主要保留指神话巨人的用法。

entries.definition: The Atlantic and eastern Pacific name for a tropical cyclone; identical in structure, different in basin.
entries.definitionCN: 大西洋与东太平洋对热带气旋的称名；结构相同，海域不同。

entries.definition: The Indian Ocean and South Pacific name for the same class of storm, or any closed low-pressure circulation.
entries.definitionCN: 印度洋与南太平洋对同类风暴的称名，也指任何闭合低压环流。

entries.definition: A narrow, violent vortex touching the ground from a thundercloud, far smaller than a typhoon.
entries.definitionCN: 从雷暴云触地的狭窄猛烈涡旋，比台风小得多。

entries.definition: The general word for disturbed weather with strong wind; typhoon is the specific tropical subtype.
entries.definitionCN: 强风扰动天气的通称；台风是其特定的热带子类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real basin names, real fixed phrases and the real compound family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的海域名、真实固定搭配与真实复合词族，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three basins, three names: hurricane, typhoon, cyclone.
normal.cn: 三个海域三个名称：hurricane、typhoon、cyclone。

normal.en: Typhoon belongs to the western North Pacific and the South China Sea.
normal.cn: 台风属于西北太平洋与南海。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: typhoon season, typhoon warning, typhoon shelter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：台风季、台风警报、避风塘。

normal.en: Super typhoon is the stronger grade above typhoon.
normal.cn: super typhoon 是台风之上的更强等级。

normal.en: Typhoon-force winds are the strongest wind term in forecasts.
normal.cn: typhoon-force 是预报里最强的风力用语。

abstract.en: Picture a whirlpool of cloud with a calm hole at its centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一个云的漩涡，中心有一个平静的孔。

abstract.en: Picture a fishing boat hiding in a narrow cove while the sea outside boils.
abstract.cn: 想象一条渔船躲在狭窄的小湾里，外面的海在翻腾。

abstract.en: Picture a wave of criticism arriving as fast as weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵批评像天气一样迅速压过来。

examples.en: The typhoon weakened to a tropical storm before reaching the coast.
examples.cn: 台风在到达海岸之前减弱为热带风暴。

examples.en: Typhoon season in the western Pacific peaks from July to October.
examples.cn: 西北太平洋的台风季在七月到十月达到高峰。

examples.en: Boats crowded into the typhoon shelter as the signal was raised.
examples.cn: 信号升起时，船只纷纷挤进避风塘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「台轰」——台风登陆时轰然一声，风球高挂

root: 经葡萄牙语 tufão 借自阿拉伯语 ṭūfān「洪水、风暴」，更早一般推测与希腊 typhōn「旋风、提丰」有关；阿拉伯语这一环是否借自希腊语尚有争议。现代拼写与汉语「大风」相近，但是否影响拼写来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the storm from open sea to harbour: the system, its basin name, its landfall, the older broad use, the season, the shelter, the metaphor and the warning signal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着风暴从外海走到港湾：系统本身、海域名称、登陆成灾、旧时的宽泛用法、季节、避风塘、比喻义与警报信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a huge cloud spiral over warm water with a calm eye at its centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：暖水上方巨大的云螺旋，中心是平静的眼区。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND NAME: one storm physics, three basin labels; typhoon is the western Pacific label.
branches.cn: 系统与名称：一套风暴物理，三个海域标签；typhoon 是西太平洋的标签。

branches.en: EVENT AND OLD WORD: the modern disaster report and the older any-storm use are two views of the same violence.
branches.cn: 事件与旧词：现代灾害报道与旧时的泛称，是同一暴力的两种视角。

branches.en: CALENDAR AND SIGNAL: the season and the numbered warning are both administrative frames around the storm.
branches.cn: 日历与信号：季节与编号警报都是围绕风暴的行政框架。

branches.en: SHELTER: the place named after the storm it defends against.
branches.cn: 避风处：以它所抵御的风暴命名的地点。

branches.en: SOCIAL STORM: criticism and anger arrive with the same sudden force.
branches.cn: 社会风暴：批评与愤怒以同样的突然力量到来。

intro.en: Typhoon is a whole borrowed word, not an English prefix-root-suffix build. Its productive life is in compounds: super typhoon, typhoon shelter, typhoon-proof, typhoon-force.
intro.cn: typhoon 是整体借入的词，不是英语的前缀—词根—后缀结构。它的构词活力体现在复合词：super typhoon、typhoon shelter、typhoon-proof、typhoon-force。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate family here: the word travelled by Arabic and Portuguese, and Latin holds only the borrowed proper name Typhon, which is not a derivational base for the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词：这个词经阿拉伯语与葡萄牙语传来，拉丁语只有借入的专名 Typhon，而它并不是英语词的派生基础。

items.meaning: a typhoon above the top sustained-wind category
items.meaningCN: 超过最高持续风速等级的台风
items.example: Super typhoons are labelled with a separate category.
items.exampleCN: 超强台风用单独的分类标注。

items.meaning: a harbour where boats refuge from storms
items.example: The old typhoon shelter is now lined with restaurants.
items.exampleCN: 旧避风塘如今沿岸开满餐馆。

items.example: The new bridge is typhoon-proof.
Typhoon-force gusts brought down the power lines.
items.exampleCN: 台风级阵风刮倒了电线。

items.example: A typhoon-like swirl appeared on the radar.
items.exampleCN: 雷达上出现了一个台风般的涡旋。

items.structure: the terminal element of the borrowed word, not a productive suffix
items.meaningCN: 在英语中没有独立含义
items.example: No English word is built with -phoon.
items.exampleCN: 没有英语词用 -phoon 构成。

items.structure: Portuguese tufão, the immediate borrowing source
items.example: Portuguese traders carried the word east and west.
items.exampleCN: 葡萄牙商人把这个词东西传播。

items.example: The Arabic noun named a destructive flood.
items.exampleCN: 这个阿拉伯名词指毁灭性的洪水。

definition_zh: 典型的；有代表性的；特有的
definition_en: showing the usual features of a group, or happening in the usual way
core_image: 一排相似的老房子，其中一栋可以代表整条街
scene: 海边小镇的早晨，渔船一条条回港，街上飘着鱼汤的味道。A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
sceneCN: 这里 typical 是「典型的；有代表性的」（第 1 个义项：体现某一类事物共性特征）；句意为这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。可以代表整条街的那栋老房子，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 typical 加 -ly 构成，义为「典型地；通常」
由 typical 加 -ity 构成，义为「典型性」
由 typical 加前缀 a- 构成，义为「非典型的」

senses.title: The one that stands for all
senses.definition: having the features that most members of a group share
senses.definitionCN: 具有某一群体多数成员共有的特征
senses.example: A typical morning here begins with the boats coming in.
senses.exampleCN: 这里典型的早晨从渔船回港开始。
senses.why: The word points at a sample good enough to stand for the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向一个足以代表整群的样本。

senses.title: The habit that marks you
senses.definition: showing the special character of a person or thing, often in a slightly critical way
senses.definitionCN: 显示某人某物特有的性格，常略带批评意味
senses.example: It was typical of him to arrive without calling.
senses.exampleCN: 不打电话就来，正是他一贯的作风。
senses.why: If a feature is shared by a group, it can also be the mark by which one member is known.
senses.whyCN: 若某特征是群体共有，也可成为辨认某个成员的特有标记。

intro.en: Typical is built on type plus the adjective ending -ical, and means of the stamp or the class.
intro.cn: typical 由 type 加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，意为「具有这一印模的」。

items.en: Typos named a blow and the mark left by it.
items.cn: typos 指一击以及它留下的印。

items.en: Typicus appeared in late Latin for something figurative.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 typicus 指具有图像或象征意味的东西。

items.en: The ending -ical joined type to make typical in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪 -ical 与 type 结合成 typical。

items.en: Science used it for a specimen that represents a whole species.
items.cn: 科学用它指代表整个物种的标本。

items.en: Everyday speech widened it to anything usual or characteristic.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到一切寻常或有代表性的事物。

note.en: The first group shares the type stem, the second holds words of the same meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 type 词干，第二组是同义词。

entries.definition: In the usual manner.
Not usual for its group.
About current affairs.
Standing for a larger group.
Typical of a person or thing.
Happening most often.

normalIntro.en: Typical means of the type: the sample that wears the class face.
normalIntro.cn: typical 意为「属于这一类的」：长着这一类的脸的样本。

normal.en: Type plus -ical makes the adjective typical.
normal.cn: type 加 -ical 成形容词 typical。

normal.en: Typical of is the set phrase for a characteristic mark.
normal.cn: typical of 是表示「某物特有的」固定搭配。

normal.en: The a- in atypical means not.
normal.cn: atypical 里的 a- 表示「不」。

normal.en: Typically works as a sentence adverb: typically, it rained.
normal.cn: typically 常作句副词：typically, it rained。

normal.en: A typical example is chosen to speak for many.
normal.cn: 典型例子是被选来代表许多个的。

abstract.en: One plain house standing in a row of similar houses.
abstract.cn: 一排相似房屋中一栋普通的房子。

abstract.en: A sample jar labelled to represent a species.
abstract.cn: 标着物种名的标本瓶。

abstract.en: Rain arriving at the same hour every afternoon.
abstract.cn: 每天下午同一时刻到来的雨。

examples.en: This is a typical example of village architecture.
examples.cn: 这是乡村建筑的典型例子。

examples.en: It is typical of her to help without being asked.
examples.cn: 不用人求就帮忙，正是她的作风。

examples.en: Winter here is typical of the whole coast.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天代表了整个海岸一带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提皮扣」——提起皮包就能当代表的那一位，最典型。

root: 由 type（类型、印模，源自希腊语 typos 一击与印痕）加形容词词尾 -ical 构成，本义为具有该类特征的，同族词有 typically、typicality、atypical。

sensesIntro.en: First the sample that stands for its class, then the trait that marks an individual.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是能代表类别的样本，再是标记个体的特性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plain house that speaks for the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间足以代表整排的普通房子。

branches.en: The sample branch: one stands for many.
branches.cn: 样本分支：一个代表许多。

branches.en: The mark branch: the trait that names you.
branches.cn: 标记分支：能叫出你名字的特征。

branches.en: The ordinary branch: nothing unusual happens.
branches.cn: 寻常分支：没有特别的事发生。

branches.en: The judgement branch: typical can gently blame.
branches.cn: 评价分支：常带一点温和的抱怨。

branches.en: The science branch: a specimen defined by its type.
branches.cn: 科学分支：以模式标本定的物种。

intro.en: Typical is type plus -ical, and the family grows with -ly, -ity and the negative a-.
intro.cn: typical 是 type 加 -ical，词族靠 -ly、-ity 与否定前缀 a- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The late Latin adjective typicus stands behind the English form, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 英语形式背后是晚期拉丁语形容词 typicus，列在下面。

items.example: This type sells well.
It forms typical and topical.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 typical 与 topical。

items.example: A typical case.
It forms typically.
Typically it rains.
It forms typicality.
It forms atypical.
An atypical result.

definition_zh: 无处不在的；普遍存在的；广泛分布的；无孔不入的
definition_en: present, seen or found almost everywhere at the same time, so that no single place can be named as an exception
core_image: 一张城市地图上，同一个蓝色小点被盖在每一条街道、每一座车站和每一家店里
scene: 街角、地铁站、便利店门口，几乎每面墙上都贴着同一个蓝色标识，转角又是一张。Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
sceneCN: 这里指某样东西到处都能见到（第 1 个义项：无处不在）；句意为智能手机在日常生活中已无处不在。图中可辨识物件：城市地图、遍布各处的蓝色标识、地铁站与便利店。

pos.zh: 无处不在的；普遍存在的；广泛分布的

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根加表示状态的名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在；普遍存在」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「无处不在地」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在的性质」
由同一词根加生物化学名词词尾构成，义为「泛素」，因广泛存在于真核细胞而得名

senses.title: Present almost everywhere
senses.definition: found in nearly every place at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 几乎在同一时间出现在每一个地方
senses.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 智能手机在日常生活中已无处不在。
senses.why: The Latin source literally says everywhere, and the adjective keeps that flat, total coverage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源字面意思就是「到处」，形容词保留了这种平铺的、全覆盖的含义。

senses.title: A widespread phenomenon
senses.definition: a condition or practice common across many places and groups
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方与群体中普遍存在的状况或做法
senses.example: Social media use is now ubiquitous among teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 社交媒体的使用如今在青少年中普遍存在。
senses.why: When a behaviour appears in every sample, the word describes a pattern rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 当一种行为出现在每个样本里，这个词描述的就是模式，而非物件。

senses.title: A name or product everyone knows
senses.titleCN: 家喻户晓的品牌与产品
senses.definition: so widely distributed in culture that almost everyone recognizes it
senses.definitionCN: 在文化中分布极广，几乎人人都认得
senses.example: The brand became ubiquitous after one viral advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 一支爆红的广告之后，这个品牌变得家喻户晓。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for visibility: the logo is not just common but unavoidable.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词描述可见度：标识不只是常见，而是避不开。

senses.title: Technology embedded in every device
senses.definition: built into so many devices and settings that its presence is taken for granted
senses.definitionCN: 被装进太多设备与场景，以致其存在被视为理所当然
senses.example: Sensors are ubiquitous in modern buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器在现代建筑中无处不在。
senses.why: Computing gave the word a technical home: the machine is no longer a place you go to.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域给了这个词一个技术归宿：机器不再是一个你要去的地方。

senses.title: A problem found in every corner
senses.definition: a fault or difficulty that appears across many unrelated settings
senses.definitionCN: 出现在许多互不相关的场景中的缺陷或困难
senses.example: Bias in hiring is ubiquitous, though it takes different forms.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘中的偏见无处不在，只是形式不同。
senses.why: The word can carry a warning: what is everywhere is also hard to notice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以带警告：到处都有的东西，也最难被察觉。

senses.title: Signs and messages everywhere
senses.titleCN: 到处出现的标识与信息
senses.definition: advertising or notices distributed so densely that they fill the visual field
senses.definitionCN: 广告或告示密集分布，占满视野
senses.example: Advertising screens are ubiquitous in the shopping district.
senses.exampleCN: 购物区里广告屏幕无处不在。
senses.why: The physical city can be covered, and the adjective describes that coverage.
senses.whyCN: 物理城市可以被覆盖，这个形容词描述的就是这种覆盖。

senses.title: A species found across habitats
senses.definition: occurring across many habitats or regions rather than in one niche
senses.definitionCN: 出现在许多栖息地或地区，而非局限于一个生态位
senses.example: The weed is ubiquitous along the riverbank.
senses.exampleCN: 这种杂草沿河岸广泛分布。
senses.why: Ecology uses the word for range, not for number: a rare animal can still be widespread.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用这个词描述分布范围，而非数量：稀少的动物也可以是广布的。

senses.title: Influence that cannot be escaped
senses.definition: an influence or system so extensive that no area of life remains outside it
senses.definitionCN: 影响或系统扩展到没有任何生活领域在其之外
senses.example: The platform's influence is ubiquitous in local news.
senses.exampleCN: 该平台对本地新闻的影响无孔不入。
senses.why: Here the word turns from description to critique: total presence begins to feel like pressure.
senses.whyCN: 这时词从描述转向批评：全面的存在开始让人感到压迫。

senses.title: Service available at any time and place
senses.definition: access to a service that no longer depends on a fixed location
senses.definitionCN: 获取某项服务不再依赖固定地点
senses.example: Wireless access is now ubiquitous on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 无线网络如今在校园里随处可得。
senses.why: Networks made availability a background condition, which is what the word describes best.
senses.whyCN: 网络让可用性成为一种背景条件，这正是这个词最擅长描述的。

intro.en: Ubiquitous is Latin for everywhere pressed into one adjective: a root meaning where, a particle meaning ever, and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「到处」压成一个形容词：一个表示「哪里」的词根、一个表示「无论」的小品词，加一个形容词词尾。

items.en: ubi meant where, the plain interrogative and relative place word.
items.cn: ubi 意为「哪里」，是最普通的地点疑问词与关系词。

items.en: -que was an enclitic meaning and, and in this combination it gave the sense of ever or any.
items.cn: -que 是表示「和」的附缀，在这一组合中给出「无论、任何」的意思。

items.en: ubique meant everywhere, in every place, and it was used adverbially in classical Latin.
items.cn: ubique 意为「到处、在每个地方」，在古典拉丁语中作副词使用。

items.en: The abstract noun ubiquitas named the state of being everywhere.
items.cn: 抽象名词 ubiquitas 命名「无处不在」的状态。

items.en: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century; the first records are early nineteenth century and the exact year is not certain, but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词；首见记录在十九世纪初，具体年份不确定，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: Networks and mobile devices made the old word newly literal, and computing adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 网络与移动设备让这个旧词重新变得字面化，计算领域把它采纳为技术术语。

note.en: The first group shares root or shape with ubiquitous; the second group names nearby ideas of wide presence and keeps their emphasis apart.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 ubiquitous 相近；第二组是与「广泛存在」意思相邻的说法，说明中区分各自侧重。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being everywhere at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时无处不在的状态。

entries.definition: The adverb describing action or presence that reaches every place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述抵达每个地方的行动或存在。

entries.definition: A clumsy but real noun for the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指这种性质本身的一个笨重但真实的名词。

entries.definition: A small protein found throughout eukaryotic cells, named for being everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在于真核细胞中的一种小蛋白，因「到处都有」而得名。

entries.definition: Of one mind; it looks close but its root is one spirit, not every place.
entries.definitionCN: 指意见一致；形近，但其词根是「同一心意」，而非「每个地方」。

entries.definition: Common in a particular group, place or time; it stresses frequency within a setting, not presence in every setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在特定群体、地方或时期常见；强调某一场景内的频率，而非每个场景都有。

entries.definition: Distributed over a large area or many people; it stresses breadth of distribution, not the absence of exceptions.
entries.definitionCN: 指分布在大片地区或许多人中；强调分布之广，而非没有例外。

entries.definition: Present everywhere at once, often with a sense of a watching or divine presence.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在于一切地方，常带被注视或神圣临在的意味。

entries.definition: Spreading through and filling every part of something; it stresses penetration rather than coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 指渗透并充满某物的每个部分；强调渗透，而非覆盖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin where-and-ever parts, the real technology phrases and the real contrast with prevalence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「哪里＋无论」构件、真实的技术搭配，以及与 prevalent 的真实区别。

normal.en: ubi means where and -que adds ever: ubique is wherever, so ubiquitous is everywhere.
normal.cn: ubi 是「哪里」，-que 加「无论」：ubique 是「无论哪里」，所以 ubiquitous 就是「到处」。

normal.en: A map with the same dot stamped on every street shows the word better than a sentence.
normal.cn: 一张在每条街都盖上同一个小点的地图，比一句话更能说明这个词。

normal.en: Ubiquitous technology, ubiquitous computing and ubiquitous access are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 无处不在的技术、普适计算与随时随地的访问是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Prevalent means common in one setting; ubiquitous means no setting is without it.
normal.cn: prevalent 指在某一场景常见；ubiquitous 指没有一个场景缺少它。

normal.en: The noun ubiquity is the state, the adverb ubiquitously is the manner.
normal.cn: 名词 ubiquity 是状态，副词 ubiquitously 是方式。

abstract.en: What is everywhere stops being noticed; ubiquity is a kind of invisibility.
abstract.cn: 到处都有的东西不再被注意；无处不在是一种隐形。

abstract.en: A word for total coverage is also a word for no exit, which is why it can sound like a warning.
abstract.cn: 一个描述全面覆盖的词，也是描述无处可退的词，所以它听起来可能像警告。

abstract.en: The same adjective describes a helpful network and an unwanted gaze; presence itself is neutral.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既描述有用的网络，也描述不受欢迎的注视；存在本身是中性的。

examples.en: Plastic packaging is now ubiquitous in every supermarket aisle.
examples.cn: 塑料包装如今在每条超市货架间都随处可见。

examples.en: The composer's arrangements became ubiquitous in film scores of the period.
examples.cn: 这位作曲家的编曲在那个时期的电影配乐中无处不在。

examples.en: Cameras are so ubiquitous that visitors no longer notice them.
examples.cn: 摄像头多到无处不在，访客已不再注意到它们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「尤比克维特斯」——拉丁语「无论哪里」压成一个词：到处都在

root: 来自拉丁语 ubique「到处」← ubi「哪里」+ -que「无论、和」，抽象名词 ubiquitas；英语在十九世纪加形容词词尾 -ous 构成 ubiquitous。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from simple everywhere-presence through phenomena, brands, devices, problems, signs, species and influence to round-the-clock availability.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从简单的「到处都在」，经过现象、品牌、设备、问题、标识、物种与影响，最后落到全天候可得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one blue mark is stamped on every street of a city map until no blank space remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚蓝印被盖在城市地图的每条街上，直到不留一点空白。

branches.en: THE PLAIN COVERAGE: an object or a practice found in every sample.
branches.cn: 朴素覆盖：物件或做法在每个样本中都出现。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE CITY: brands and signs that fill the visual field.
branches.cn: 可见的城市：品牌与标识占满视野。

branches.en: THE EMBEDDED NETWORK: sensors and access that no longer need a fixed place.
branches.cn: 嵌入的网络：传感器与访问不再依赖固定地点。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE RANGE: a fault everywhere, a species across every habitat.
branches.cn: 模式与范围：到处都有的缺陷，跨越每种栖息地的物种。

branches.en: THE TOTAL GAZE: influence with no area left outside it.
branches.cn: 全面注视：没有任何领域留在其外的影响。

intro.en: Ubiquitous is three Latin pieces and one adjective ending: a place word, an ever particle, and a suffix of quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是三个拉丁部件加一个形容词词尾：一个地点词、一个「无论」小品词，以及一个表性质的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies ubi, ubique and ubiquitas; English adds -ous to make the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 ubi、ubique 与 ubiquitas；英语加上 -ous 构成形容词。

items.example: The place question begins the word.
items.exampleCN: 地点疑问词开启了这个词。

items.example: It turns where into wherever.
items.exampleCN: 它把「哪里」变成「无论哪里」。

items.example: The adverb states total coverage.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词陈述全面覆盖。

items.example: The abstract noun names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词命名这种性质。

items.example: It forms the English adjective.
The noun drops the adjective ending for a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 名词去掉形容词词尾，换成状态名词。

items.example: It forms ubiquitously.
It forms ubiquitousness.
It forms ubiquitin, named for wide presence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ubiquitin，因广泛存在而得名。

derivatives.zh: 由词根加状态名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「无处不在地」
由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「无处不在的性质」
由词根加科学名词词尾构成，义为「泛素」

definition_zh: 最终的；最后的；根本的；极限的；终极的
definition_en: coming at the very end, or being the most basic and extreme form of something
core_image: 一条长路的尽头，最后一面旗插在那里
scene: 登山队在长坡上走了整整一天，抬头时终于看见最后那道山脊上立着界碑。Reaching the summit was the ultimate test of their patience.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimate 是「最终的、终极的」（第 1 个义项：处于最后位置）；句意为登顶是他们对耐心最彻底的考验。长路尽头的那面旗正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「最终；归根到底」
同源名词，义为「最后通牒」
形容词加 -acy 构成名词，义为「终极性；根本性」

senses.title: Coming at the very end
senses.definition: happening or coming at the end of a long process
senses.definitionCN: 发生或出现在一个漫长过程的末尾
senses.example: The ultimate decision rests with the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 最终的决定权在委员会手里。
senses.why: Latin ultimus is the superlative of ulterior, meaning farther, so ultimate is literally the farthest point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ultimus 是 ulterior（更远的）的最高级，因此 ultimate 字面上就是「最远的那个点」。

senses.title: Most basic and fundamental
senses.definition: being the basic cause or the power behind everything else
senses.definitionCN: 作为其他一切背后的根本原因或力量
senses.example: The ultimate cause of the failure was poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 失败的根本原因是计划不当。
senses.why: At the farthest point you reach the bottom of things, so the last item in a chain becomes the root of it.
senses.whyCN: 走到最远的尽头就触及了事物的底，于是链条的最后一环成了它的根。

senses.title: The best or most extreme example
senses.definition: the finest or most complete example of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类中最好、最完整的例子
senses.example: This little car is the ultimate city vehicle.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆小车是城市用车的极致。
senses.why: Whatever stands at the far end of a scale is the extreme, and the extreme reads as perfection.
senses.whyCN: 处在刻度最远一端的即是极端，而极端常被读成完美。

senses.title: Highest in authority
senses.definition: holding the highest power, with no one above
senses.definitionCN: 掌握最高权力，其上无人
senses.example: The ultimate authority on the rules is the court.
senses.exampleCN: 规则的最终权威是法院。
senses.why: A chain of command is also a line, and the person at its far end cannot be overruled.
senses.whyCN: 指挥链也是一条线，站在最远端的人无法再被推翻。

senses.title: The finest point of something
senses.definition: the most developed state that something can reach
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所能达到的最成熟状态
senses.example: This chair is the ultimate in simple design.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子是简约设计的顶点。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun that names the far end itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词，直接指称那条线的远端。

intro.en: The word comes straight from Latin and keeps its superlative shape.
intro.cn: 这个词直接来自拉丁语，至今保留最高级形态。

items.en: Ulter means beyond, and its comparative ulterior means farther.
items.cn: ulter 意为「在那边」，其比较级 ulterior 意为「更远的」。

items.en: Ultimus is the superlative, the farthest or last, and gives nouns such as ultimus finis, the last boundary.
items.cn: ultimus 是最高级，意为「最远的、最后的」，构成 ultimus finis（最后的边界）等说法。

items.en: Late Latin ultimatus is a participle formed on ultimus, meaning brought to the end.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 ultimatus 由 ultimus 构成的动词分词，意为「被带到尽头」。

items.en: English takes ultimate in the seventeenth century for what comes last.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ultimate，指居于最后之物。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of the most extreme or finest case.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了「最极端、最出色」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ult- stem, and the near-meaning group gathers words about endings and extremes.
note.cn: 形近组共用 ult- 词干，近义组汇集表示结尾与极致之词。

a final demand backed by threats

normalIntro.en: The word is the superlative of a Latin word for beyond, so it always carries the picture of a far end.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「更远」一词的最高级，因此总带着「最远端」的画面。

normal.en: Ultimus is the Latin superlative for farthest, and -ate marks it as an adjective in English.
normal.cn: ultimus 是拉丁语「最远」的最高级，-ate 让它成为英语形容词。

normal.en: Ultimately is the adverb and means in the end or at bottom.
normal.cn: ultimately 是副词，意为最终、说到底。

normal.en: An ultimatum is the last word that ends a negotiation.
normal.cn: ultimatum 是结束谈判的最后那句话。

normal.en: Ulterior motives lie beyond the surface, on the far side of what is said.
normal.cn: ulterior motives 藏在表面之外，在话语的另一边。

normal.en: The ultimate goal is the one every other step serves.
normal.cn: ultimate goal 是其他每一步都为之服务的那一个。

abstract.en: Trace a long line to its last centimetre and plant a flag there.
abstract.cn: 把一条长线画到最后一厘米，在那里插一面旗。

abstract.en: Notice that the flag also marks the deepest cause, not only the end.
abstract.cn: 注意这面旗不只标终点，也标最深的根。

abstract.en: Turn the same scale around and see everything piled up at one extreme.
abstract.cn: 再把刻度翻过来，看见一切都堆在一个顶端。

examples.en: Their ultimate aim was to make the service free.
examples.cn: 他们的最终目的是让这项服务免费。

examples.en: He is ultimately responsible for the whole team.
examples.cn: 最终要为整个团队负责的是他。

examples.en: For many cooks, this knife is the ultimate in simplicity.
examples.cn: 在很多厨师眼里，这把刀就是简约的极致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特妹」——奥特曼的妹妹总是站在队伍最末尾，最后一个出场。

root: 拉丁语 ulter（在那边）、比较级 ulterior（更远的）、最高级 ultimus（最远的、最后的），晚期拉丁语 ultimatus 进入英语；同族有 ultimately、ultimatum

sensesIntro.en: All senses place something at the far end of a line, whether a process, a cause, a scale, or a hierarchy.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都把某物放在一条线的远端：过程的尾、原因的根、刻度的端，或等级的顶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag standing at the last point of a long road.
core.cn: 核心意象：长路最后一点上立着的一面旗。

branches.en: The time branch: what happens after everything else.
branches.cn: 时间分支：在其他一切之后发生的事。

branches.en: The cause branch: what lies under all the other reasons.
branches.cn: 原因分支：压在其他理由下面的那一层。

branches.en: The quality branch: the extreme example and its noun form.
branches.cn: 程度分支：极端的范例及其名词形式。

branches.en: The power branch: the top of a chain of command.
branches.cn: 权力分支：指挥链的最顶端。

branches.en: The everyday sense in which a goal or a decision comes last.
branches.cn: 日常义：目标或决定排在最后。

intro.en: The word is a Latin superlative stem dressed as an English adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语最高级词干披上英语形容词外衣。

latinIntro.en: The ulter family clusters around the idea of beyond.
latinIntro.cn: ulter 这一族词都围绕「在那边」的意思。

items.example: The stem comes from ultimus.
Ultimate keeps the Latin stem as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: ultimate 以形容词身份保留拉丁词干。

items.example: Ultimate gives ultimately.
Ultimatum names a final demand.
An ulterior reason stays out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 别有用心的理由藏在看不见处。

items.example: The ultimatum expired at noon.
Ultimately the plan failed.
They questioned the ultimacy of the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这条规则的终极性。

definition_zh: 紫外线的；紫外区的；紫外线辐射（不可数）
definition_en: relating to the band of radiation just beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum, with shorter waves and higher energy
core_image: 石英灯发出看不见的短波光，培养皿里的菌落几分钟后全部失活
scene: 实验台上石英灯发出看不见的短波光，几分钟后培养皿里的菌落全部失活。A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 ultraviolet 指「波长比紫光更短、肉眼看不见的那段辐射」（第 1 个义项：位于可见光谱紫端之外的高能短波辐射）；句意为石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。可辨识物件：石英灯、培养皿、菌落、护目镜。

senses.title: The band beyond violet
senses.titleCN: 紫光之外的那段不可见辐射
senses.definition: the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths shorter than visible violet but longer than X-rays
senses.definitionCN: 电磁波谱中波长比可见紫光更短、比 X 射线更长的区域
senses.example: A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。
senses.why: ultra- means beyond, so the name places this band past violet on the ordered scale of colours.
senses.whyCN: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此这个名字把这一段放在颜色次序中紫之外。

senses.title: Sunlight ultraviolet
senses.definition: the short-wave component of sunlight that reaches the ground after the atmosphere filters much of it
senses.definitionCN: 阳光中被大气滤去大半后仍到达地面的短波成分
senses.example: Sunlight ultraviolet darkens the pigment in skin.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光中的紫外线使皮肤中的色素变深。
senses.why: the sun is the everyday source, so the band is usually met as a component of daylight rather than as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 太阳是最日常的来源，因此这一段通常作为日光的一部分被遇见，而不是作为灯。

senses.title: Sterilising ultraviolet
senses.titleCN: 用于杀菌消毒的紫外线
senses.definition: the use of short-wave ultraviolet to damage the genetic material of microbes and stop them reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 用短波紫外破坏微生物遗传物质、使其无法繁殖
senses.example: Ultraviolet treatment cleared the water of bacteria within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外线处理几分钟内就清除了水中的细菌。
senses.why: the same short waves that damage skin also damage microbial DNA, so the band becomes a tool.
senses.whyCN: 伤害皮肤的短波同样会损伤微生物的遗传物质，于是这一段成了工具。

senses.title: Ultraviolet astronomy
senses.titleCN: 紫外天文学：观测高温天体
senses.definition: the observation of hot stars and gas through their ultraviolet emission, which the atmosphere blocks from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 借高温恒星与气体的紫外辐射进行观测，而大气在地面挡住了这些辐射
senses.example: Ultraviolet astronomy must be done from orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外天文学必须从轨道上进行。
senses.why: only very hot objects emit strongly in this band, and the atmosphere absorbs it, so the technique needs space.
senses.whyCN: 只有非常高温的物体在这一段强烈辐射，而大气又吸收它，因此这项技术需要太空。

senses.title: The ultraviolet index
senses.titleCN: 紫外线指数：衡量到达地面的强度
senses.definition: a scale reporting the intensity of burning ultraviolet at the surface on a given day
senses.definitionCN: 报告某日地表灼伤性紫外线强度的指数
senses.example: The ultraviolet index reached eleven at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时紫外线指数达到十一。
senses.why: a public warning needs a number, and the number is reported under the band name.
senses.whyCN: 公共警示需要一个数字，而这个数字就以该波段的名字发布。

senses.title: Ultraviolet absorbance
senses.titleCN: 紫外吸光度：光谱分析中的读数
senses.definition: the amount of ultraviolet a sample absorbs, used to infer concentration or electronic structure
senses.definitionCN: 样品所吸收的紫外量，用来推断浓度或电子结构
senses.example: The ultraviolet absorbance told them how much protein the solution held.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度让他们知道溶液中有多少蛋白质。
senses.why: many molecules absorb specific ultraviolet wavelengths, so a single reading can measure what is present.
senses.whyCN: 许多分子会吸收特定的紫外波长，因此一次读数就能测出存在的东西。

senses.title: Ultraviolet curing
senses.titleCN: 紫外固化：用紫外光使涂层硬化
senses.definition: the curing of inks, resins or adhesives by ultraviolet light that triggers a chemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用紫外光触发化学反应，使油墨、树脂或胶黏剂硬化
senses.example: Ultraviolet curing sets the printing ink in under a second.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外固化在不到一秒内就让印刷油墨定形。
senses.why: the high energy of the band starts reactions that heat alone would take far longer to start.
senses.whyCN: 这一段的高能量能启动单靠加热要慢得多的反应。

senses.title: Abstract: an invisible part of a range
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：一个范围中看不见却起作用的部分
senses.definition: the portion of any range that lies past its obvious limit and still has effects, though it cannot be seen directly
senses.definitionCN: 任何范围中超出明显边界、虽不能直接看见却仍起作用的那部分
senses.example: The costs were the ultraviolet of the budget, invisible but damaging.
senses.exampleCN: 这些成本是预算中看不见的紫外部分，无形却有伤害。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the position beyond the visible edge, where effect outruns sight.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「在可见边缘之外」这个位置：效果超出视觉所能及。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin-English hybrid: ultra, beyond, plus the English colour word violet. It dates from the 1840s, after chemical effects beyond violet were found.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁与英语的混合词：拉丁 ultra「超出」加英语颜色词 violet。它出现于 1840 年代，在紫光之外的化学效应被发现之后。

items.en: Ultra meant beyond or on the far side, and English uses it as the prefix ultra-, as in ultrasonic and ultramarine.
items.cn: ultra 意为「超出、在远侧」，英语以 ultra- 作前缀，如 ultrasonic 与 ultramarine。

items.en: Violet goes back through Old French to Latin viola, the violet flower; the colour name is older than the physics.
items.cn: violet 经古法语上溯到拉丁 viola「堇菜」；颜色名比物理学用法更早。

items.en: Ritter found that silver salts darkened fastest beyond the violet end of a prism spectrum, showing a chemical effect where nothing was visible.
items.cn: 里特尔发现银盐在棱镜光谱紫端之外变黑最快，说明在看不见之处仍有化学作用。

items.en: The English adjective ultraviolet was formed in the 1840s, once the invisible band needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 英语形容词 ultraviolet 于 1840 年代成形，因为这段不可见波段需要一个自己的名字。

items.en: Sterilisation, the ozone layer, the ultraviolet index and curing all became familiar in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 杀菌、臭氧层、紫外线指数与固化都在 20 世纪变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first use of ultraviolet is not agreed; ultra and viola are well attested Latin words, so no root uncertainty attaches to either half.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：ultraviolet 的确切首用无定论；ultra 与 viola 都是有据的拉丁词，因此两半都不存在词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds the boundary words that look alike because they share ultra-; group two holds the neighbouring bands and the effects people confuse with them.
note.cn: 第一组是因共享 ultra- 而形近的边界词；第二组是相邻波段以及人们容易混淆的效应。

entries.definition: Infra- means below, so infrared lies past the red end with longer waves and lower energy.
entries.definitionCN: infra- 意为「在下」，因此红外在红端之外，波长更长、能量更低。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus marine: a deep blue pigment once shipped from beyond the sea, with nothing to do with radiation.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「海」：一种曾从海外运来的深蓝颜料，与辐射无关。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus sound: vibrations above hearing, used in scanning and cleaning.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「声」：高于听觉的振动，用于扫描与清洗。

entries.definition: An instrument that reveals particles too small for an ordinary microscope by scattering light sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 靠侧向散射光显示普通显微镜看不见的微粒的仪器。

entries.definition: The last visible colour before the band begins; it is the boundary ultraviolet is named against.
entries.definitionCN: 该波段开始前最后一个可见颜色；紫外线正是以它为界命名。

entries.definition: Radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms; short ultraviolet belongs to this class.
entries.definitionCN: 能量足以把电子从原子中剥离的辐射；短波紫外属于这一类。

entries.definition: The band beyond ultraviolet, with even shorter waves and enough energy to pass through tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 紫外之外的那一段，波长更短，能量足以穿过组织。

entries.definition: The whole solar spectrum at the surface, of which ultraviolet is the part that burns.
entries.definitionCN: 地表的整个太阳光谱，其中造成灼伤的那部分就是紫外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prefix, the real experiment and the real public uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀、真实的实验与真实的公共用途。

normal.en: ultra- means beyond, so ultraviolet is the band beyond violet.
normal.cn: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此紫外是紫之外的那一段。

normal.en: Violet comes from Latin viola, the flower, so the colour name came first.
normal.cn: 紫色一词出自拉丁 viola「堇菜」，所以颜色名先于物理术语。

normal.en: The abbreviation UV is standard in labels and forecasts.
normal.cn: 两个字母的缩写在标签与预报中是标准写法。

normal.en: It both burns and sterilises, because short waves damage genetic material.
normal.cn: 它既灼伤也能杀菌，因为短波会损伤遗传物质。

normal.en: Near ultraviolet and far ultraviolet are the two subdivisions.
normal.cn: 近紫外与远紫外是两个分区。

abstract.en: Picture a room lit by a lamp everyone insists is off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，人人都说灯关了，屋里却仍亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that only the skin can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有皮肤读得懂的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a cost that never appears on any invoice but still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔从不出现在任何账单上、却仍然到来的成本。

examples.en: The ozone layer absorbs most ultraviolet before it reaches the ground.
examples.cn: 臭氧层在紫外线到达地面之前吸收了其中大部分。

examples.en: Ultraviolet lamps sterilise the air inside the hospital ward.
examples.cn: 紫外灯对病房内的空气进行杀菌。

examples.en: The forecast put the ultraviolet index at eight, high enough to burn in minutes.
examples.cn: 预报的紫外线指数为八，足以在几分钟内晒伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ultra（超出）+ violet（紫）」——排在紫色之外的那一段 → 紫外线

root: 拉丁 ultra「超出」+ 英语 violet（经古法语上溯拉丁 viola「堇菜」）；两半均为有据来源，无重构词根。英语 ultraviolet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin at the band, then move to sunlight, sterilising, astronomy, the public index, absorbance, curing and finally the unseen part of any range.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从波段本身开始，随后走向阳光、杀菌、天文、公共指数、吸光度、固化，最后落在任何范围中看不见的那一部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that shows nothing yet empties a dish of living colonies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏看不见光的灯，却让一皿活菌落全部失活。

branches.en: POSITION: the prefix fixes the address past violet, and everything else follows from that place.
branches.cn: 位置：前缀把地址定在紫之外，其余义项都从这个位置而来。

branches.en: DAYLIGHT AND WARNING: the sun supplies it, and a number warns how much arrives.
branches.cn: 日光与警示：太阳提供它，一个数字警告来了多少。

branches.en: CONTROL: the same energy kills microbes and hardens resins.
branches.cn: 控制：同一份能量既能杀死微生物，也能使树脂硬化。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: hot stars and absorbing molecules are both read through this band.
branches.cn: 测量：高温恒星与吸收分子都通过这一段被读取。

branches.en: METAPHOR: whatever lies past the visible edge but still acts.
branches.cn: 比喻：位于可见边缘之外却仍然起作用的一切。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin prefix on a colour word of Latin descent, so both halves have a traceable history.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁前缀加一个源自拉丁的颜色词，两半都有可追溯的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultra means beyond; Latin viola gives violet through French. The modern compound itself is nineteenth-century English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ultra 意为「超出」；拉丁 viola 经法语给出 violet。这个近代复合词本身是十九世纪英语的产物。

items.example: The prefix places the band beyond violet.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该波段放在紫之外。

items.structure: violet (English colour word, from Old French violette, from Latin viola)
items.example: Violet is the boundary of the visible band.
items.exampleCN: 紫色是可见波段的边界。

items.example: The lamp emits ultraviolet.

items.meaning: the part closest to visible violet
items.meaningCN: 最靠近可见紫光的那部分
items.example: Near-ultraviolet light is used in some detectors.
items.exampleCN: 近紫外光用于某些探测器。

items.example: Far-ultraviolet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere.
items.exampleCN: 远紫外光在大气高层被吸收。

items.meaning: a lamp made to emit ultraviolet
items.example: The ultraviolet lamp sterilised the bench.
items.exampleCN: 紫外灯对台面做了杀菌。

items.meaning: a public scale of ultraviolet intensity
items.meaningCN: 紫外线强度的公共指数
items.example: The ultraviolet index warned of strong sun.
items.exampleCN: 紫外线指数提示阳光很强。

items.example: Ultraviolet spectroscopy measured the protein.
items.exampleCN: 紫外光谱法测出了蛋白质。

items.meaning: how much ultraviolet a sample takes in
items.example: The ultraviolet absorbance rose with concentration.
items.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度随浓度升高。
